issues.legal_issue: The time allowed for making a deposit required to seek the setting aside of an execution sale is distinct from the time allowed for filing the application.
material_facts: Immovable property was sold in execution of a decree, and an application was made to set aside the sale on deposit under Order XXI Rule 89.
The High Court treated a deposit made within the application period as timely, relying on the longer period for filing an application.
The appeal by the auction-purchaser challenged that conclusion.
issues.conclusion: The deposit required under Order XXI Rule 89 had to be made within 30 days of the sale; the 60-day period for making the application under Article 127 did not extend the deposit period. The Court set aside the High Court’s ruling on limitation and allowed the appeal to that extent.
issues.legal_principle: Order XXI Rule 89 makes deposit a condition precedent to an application to set aside an execution sale, and Rule 92(2) requires that deposit within 30 days of the sale. Article 127 of the Limitation Act, 1963 governs the period for making the application, not the deposit. The provisions prescribe separate periods for separate steps and are not inconsistent. Clear statutory language should be applied without adding or supplying words; the Court may address a manifest contradiction with legislative purpose but may not repair an omission where the text is clear. The Court relied on Nalinakhya Bysack v. Shyam Sunder Haldar, Mersey Docks v. Henderson, Crawford v. Spooner, Seaford Court Estates v. Asher, and M. Pentiah v. Muddala Veeramallappa; it rejected the contrary approach in Basavantappa v. Gangadhar Narayan Dharwadkar and noted that Dakshayini v. Madhavan’s view about a more practical period was for the legislature to address.

predicates.execution_sale_challenge: A person seeks to set aside a sale of property conducted to execute a decree.
predicates.deposit_precedes_application: The applicable procedure requires the person seeking to set aside the sale to make a deposit before making the application.
predicates.different_deadlines_apply: The applicable rules prescribe one deadline for the required deposit and a different deadline for filing the application.

issues.definition: When an execution-sale challenge requires a deposit before an application and separate deadlines govern those steps, the deposit deadline operates independently of the application deadline.
